title: In one longitudinal sample, 76 percent of infants showed a vocabulary spurt
summary: Gomez Diaz and colleagues found a vocabulary spurt in 76 percent of 45 infants, in at least one way of counting words.
body: Miranda Gomez Diaz, Laia Fibla, Rachel Ka-Ying Tsui, and Krista Byers-Heinlein followed 45 infants in Quebec, learning English, French, or both, from 16 to 30 months, with vocabulary measured 617 times. They fit a logistic curve and counted a spurt at the curve's midpoint. Seventy-six percent of the infants showed a spurt in at least one vocabulary type: one language, concepts across languages, or words summed across languages. The paper says a spurt is not found in every study and that the share depends on how a spurt is defined. This 76 percent is their sample under their curve, not a law for every child.

sources.title: Testing Theories of the Vocabulary Spurt with Monolingual and Bilingual Infants
sources.author: Miranda Gomez Diaz, Laia Fibla, Rachel Ka-Ying Tsui, and Krista Byers-Heinlein
sources.note: Opened 2026-11-26 at the PMC page. Supports the abstract's 76 percent figure, the sample of 45 infants and 617 measurements, and the paper's discussion that other studies do not all find a spurt.

said_by: Gomez Diaz, Fibla, Tsui, and Byers-Heinlein
